aspects.says: ORDER BY ? binds a value, not a column name: H2 reads it as a column number, and another database may sort every row by the same constant.
basis: section:A Bind Parameter Holds a Value, So a Sort Column Comes from an Allow-List
aspects.reason: what a bound ORDER BY parameter does differs between databases; a graded test could only pin H2's error, which the page shows as a run

aspects.says: A cast or check after readObject comes after every class's own readObject has run; an ObjectInputFilter set on the stream is asked about each class, nested ones too, before it is built.
basis: section:Check Classes With a Filter Before readObject Builds Them, Not the Result After

aspects.says: A requested path stays inside its base only if the resolved path is normalized and then compared with Path.startsWith; without normalize() .. escapes, and a string prefix accepts a sibling directory whose name begins like the base.
basis: section:A `..` Escapes the Base Unless the Check Normalizes the Path and Compares Elements

aspects.says: Input pasted after ORDER BY can read hidden data through the order of the rows, and on H2 a semicolon runs a second statement.
basis: section:A Bind Parameter Holds a Value, So a Sort Column Comes from an Allow-List

aspects.says: A sort column or direction can't be a bind parameter, so the code maps each documented sort key to SQL text it wrote itself and refuses anything else; an identifier-shaped check still lets through real columns the API doesn't expose.
basis: section:A Bind Parameter Holds a Value, So a Sort Column Comes from an Allow-List

aspects.says: normalize() never reads the disk, so a symbolic link inside the base can lead outside it; toRealPath() follows links, and the base must be compared as a real path too.
basis: section:A Symlink Inside the Base Points Anywhere; Check the Real Path

aspects.says: A filter that answers UNDECIDED leaves the class allowed when no JVM-wide filter is set, so an allow-list filter ends by rejecting everything else (!*); jdk.serialFilter sets the JVM-wide filter.
basis: section:Check Classes With a Filter Before readObject Builds Them, Not the Result After

aspects.says: The JDK's default DocumentBuilderFactory reads a file named by an external entity into the result; disallow-doctype-decl, or ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD set to "", refuses it.
basis: section:The JDK's XML Parsers Read External Entities Until You Turn Them Off

aspects.says: SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory and TransformerFactory read the same external entity by default, and each factory is configured on its own.
basis: section:The JDK's XML Parsers Read External Entities Until You Turn Them Off
aspects.reason: the same mechanism as the DOM factory that order-import grades; a second practice per factory would repeat it

aspects.says: Turning off external general entities leaves parameter entities reading files, and setExpandEntityReferences(false) still opens the file.
basis: section:The JDK's XML Parsers Read External Entities Until You Turn Them Off
